title: Podcast scenes in the show's own look (stage, waveform, punchline, quote, topic, reaction, lower third)
what_it_does: Writes the scene blocks that make an audio-only podcast a picture: a looping stage (the show's cover or ground, slow motion) with a speaker plate per host that lights up when that host talks, a waveform drawn from pre-computed levels, big kinetic punchline words, a host-attributed quote, a chapter title, hand-drawn reaction marks and a host lower third. 16:9 and 9:16; colours and fonts from frame.md and its `podcast:` block; the `ink-sketch` and `clean` looks are CSS classes of the same templates.
when_to_use: For the podcast lane (see docs/lanes/PODCAST.md): the agent writes scenes.json from the transcript, then assemble-long --audio renders it. Use ink-sketch for a black-and-white line-art show, clean for a plain one. Not for talking-head footage (use overlay-cards) and not for charts or numbers (not built yet).
notes: Everything is drawn from the show's own colours, fonts and shapes: no emoji fonts, no stock or meme images. The cover art is baked once with ffmpeg (inverted when it is white paper under a dark brand, soft-edged). Fonts are fetched and embedded by HyperFrames from the family names in frame.md. The waveform block (HTML) is for short pieces; assemble-long's audio mode draws the always-on waveform natively from the same levels because a 60-minute Chrome render of it would be far too slow. Proof: example/run-proof.sh.
